scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Finite triangular approximation of radial sweeps” (preprints/Finite-triangular-approximation-of-radial-sweeps-September-27-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 100 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6e7f63022190f390), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the data in (1.1), suppose that w′ (t) = λ(t)(a + tb) (t ∈ J) for a continuous real function λ. For any finite partition α = t0 < t1 < · · · < tN = β, put Ii = [ti−1, ti] and choose arbitrary tags ci ∈ Ii. There are N cylinders covering S, with axes parallel to e + w(ci) and nondegenerate compact triangular perpendicular bases. These covers can be chosen so that their total base area tends to A as the mesh δ = maxi |Ii| tends to zero, uniformly over the partitions and tags. Alternatively, take each base to be the perpendicular projection of the actual compact sweep with t ∈ Ii, in the same frozen direction e + w(ci). These N cylinders cover S, and their total base area also tends to A, uniformly over the partitions and tags.
